From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Systems — post-demo integration qualification & next steps

Hi Ben / Alyssa,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — appreciate the deep context on your conversational support workflow. Quick recap from our side so we have a shared set of priorities and clear next steps.

Key pain points you called out:
- Current system has inconsistent latency under load (spikes to 1.2s for short chats, up to 3s for longer RAG flows) which degrades agent UX.
- Embedding-based reranking is core to NLU accuracy; you see a 12% drop in top-1 match after migrating models.
- Need reliable function-calling to execute domain ops (ticket lookup, CSM note write) with strict structured outputs (JSON schema) to avoid downstream parsing errors.
- Security: VPC-only access for inference, audit logs for data residency, and SOC2 evidence are gating items for procurement.

Goals we discussed:
- PoC to validate streaming low-latency chat + function-calls within two weeks.
- Prototype reranking pipeline using Redwood embeddings + a small candidate set to measure improvement on your bench.
- Pricing/scale: determine whether Hosted API is sufficient or you need Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.

Technical fit notes (high level):
- Streaming + function calling: Redwood supports streaming token-by-token with function-calling hooks. We’ll show an example where the model emits a validated JSON object before final message.
- Embeddings & rerank: we recommend a quick A/B between your current embedding model and Redwood-verified 1536-d embeddings for rerank tests.
- Caching: prefix KV caching will help reduce repeated context cost for agent state.

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses):
1) Share a one-page Mutual Action Plan (attached) with milestones for PoC + demo cadence (Stephanie).
2) Internal deep-dive: engineering will pair with your infra lead to confirm VPC/networking and security requirements (Jonas).
3) Demo + sample dataset: you to send a sanitized sample of 200 chat sessions or allow us to sample from staging (Ben/Alyssa).
4) Pricing checklist: we’ll put together a ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated including expected token volumes (Rishi).

Attachments: redwood-aurora-mvp-map.xlsx (MAP), redwood-functioncall-demo-plan.pdf (demo plan).

Proposed times for technical deep-dive next week (PT): Mon 04/26 10:00–11:00, Tue 04/27 13:00–14:00. Let me know what works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to moving to a quick PoC.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying items from our engineering side before we lock a deep-dive: 

1) Function-calling reliability: what are typical failure modes if a downstream API (ticketing) is slow? Do you support automatic retries or idempotency tokens for called functions?

2) KV cache & state: when you say "prefix KV caching" — is that persisted per-user session? How do you handle eviction for long-running sessions?

3) Embedding dims & storage: what vector size do you recommend for our rerank use-case (we currently use 1024-d) and do you provide turnkey vector store connectors or do we manage index hosting?

4) Security artifacts: can you share SOC2 Type II evidence and an outline of your VPC/on-prem options for inference? Our security team will need to start a questionnaire.

We can aim for Mon 04/26 10:00 for the deep-dive — that time works for our infra lead (Alyssa). I’ll coordinate sharing a redacted sample dataset today.

Thanks,
Ben Turner

Hi Ben / Alyssa —

Thanks — Mon 04/26 10:00 PT is confirmed on our side. Calendar invite sent.

Quick answers while Jonas prepares the deep-dive:
- Function-calls: Redwood provides configurable retry policies and idempotency tokens; if a downstream API times out we can either surface a partial response or automatically retry up to N times before returning a structured failure object (configurable). Jonas will include example schemas.
- KV cache: cache can be per-session with configurable TTLs; long-running sessions we recommend a sliding TTL of 12–24 hours with a max memory cap and LRU eviction. We’ll show tuning knobs in the deep-dive.
- Embeddings: 1536-d is typically a good starting point for rerank; we also support 1024/2048 and can run a quick A/B for you. We provide first-party connectors for common vector stores and can run the index in our Dedicated environment if you want Redwood-managed indexing.
- Security: attaching our SOC2 summary + a short note on VPC/private options. For the procurement questionnaire, please add me and Rishi and we’ll respond.

Attached: redwood-aurora-mvp-map.xlsx; redwood-functioncall-demo-plan.pdf

See you Monday — will follow up after the tech session with a draft MAP timeline and pricing sketch.

Best,
Stephanie
